notes: Executable Fixin and Vougeot vineyard-law constraints directly observable in VineyardBlock. Boolean compliance rules are kept separate from dead/missing-vine yield adjustments. Conventional row vine spacing uses an inclusive 0.50 m minimum; plantation en foule uses the source's strict greater-than-0.50 m rule. The 20% dead/missing-vine trigger comes from each appellation specification, while the proportional yield remedy comes independently from Code rural D.645-4.

fr_code_rural_d645_4.title: Code rural et de la pêche maritime, article D.645-4
fr_code_rural_d645_4.scope: For AOC vineyard parcels, once the appellation-specific dead/missing-vine threshold is exceeded, the authorized yield entering the claimable AOC volume is reduced proportionally to the percentage of dead or missing vines.

constraints.notes: Current Fixin specification. General pruning paths are executable. Fixin also permits Guyot double during the two-year cordon-establishment period with at most five buds on each long cane; that conditional exception remains unresolved until cordon-establishment and per-cane state are modeled. Extra retained buds under otherwise permitted pruning remain conditionally compliant only when fruiting shoots at 11-12 leaves do not exceed the ordinary pruning ceiling. Conventional rows allow vine spacing at 0.50 m; foule requires spacing strictly greater than 0.50 m. The appellation specifies a 20% dead/missing-vine trigger; the quantitative reduction above that trigger is applied separately under Code rural D.645-4.

Current INAO-linked Vougeot specification. Red vines use the reviewed eight-bud ceiling for the listed short-pruning systems or Guyot simple; white cordon paths permit ten buds and white Guyot simple eight. Extra retained buds require a compliant fruiting-shoot count at 11-12 leaves. Conventional trellised canopy height is at least 0.6 times row spacing; foule requires stakes. Conventional rows allow vine spacing at 0.50 m; foule requires spacing strictly greater than 0.50 m. The appellation specifies a 20% dead/missing-vine trigger; the quantitative reduction above that trigger is applied separately under Code rural D.645-4.
